content.introduction: The sources indicate that the S&P 500 is currently experiencing robust mid-term trend conditions with a bullish outlook, as the market closed above its 100-day moving average and the majority of index constituents are trading above their 100-day and 150-day moving averages. The regime has flipped from Risk-On to Risk-Off, with a 91.3% probability of remaining in Risk-Off territory over the next five trading days. The forecast for the end of 2026 suggests a base range of 7,800–8,100, with earnings growth remaining supportive but various factors like valuations, inflation, and Federal Reserve policy potentially impacting the outlook. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding specific future movements beyond this range.
body:
Mid-term TREND conditions remain robust, holding at their maximum reading. The WSC Trend Index continues to indicate broad-based strength, with a high percentage of stocks trading above their 52-week highs. The WSC Mid-Term Price Trend remains bullish, and the market closed above its 100-day moving average, with the EMA 100 Line still rising. Participation metrics such as the Percentage of Stocks Above 100-Day MA and 150-Day MA both confirm that the majority of index constituents are in [...] The current combination of Short-Term and Mid-Term Market Health situates the regime as very stable, with a 91.3% probability of remaining in Risk-Off territory over the next five trading days (Increasing Risk 89.1%, High Risk 2.2%). [...] The regime flipped from Risk-On (Very High Reward) to Risk-Off (Increasing Risk) today, ending a one-day run of the prior regime.
 Tomorrow's regime-retention probability is 91%, with an 89% chance of remaining in Increasing Risk; five-day regime change probability stands at 39%.
 Seven indicators flipped today, three in Trend, three in Trend Quality, and one in Sentiment, while all dimensions saw activity.

This S&P 500 Forecast uses a 7,800–8,100 base range for the end of 2026, balanced against meaningful bear and bull scenarios. Earnings growth remains supportive, but valuations, inflation, Treasury yields, Federal Reserve policy and narrow megacap leadership can change the outlook quickly. The 2027 and 2030 ranges are wider because each additional year introduces more uncertainty. Technical levels can help traders monitor the near-term trend, but they do not guarantee future prices.
